title: Two What? Physical Quantities Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A doctor checks your temperature, a shopkeeper weighs rice, a student measures a table. Three different jobs, one same idea. And a recipe card that says "sugar: 2" shows why a number alone means nothing. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 1, Units and Measurement) we learn what a physical quantity is and the two big ways physicists sort them.

You will measure one pencil on a live measuring bench in millimetres, centimetres and metres and watch the number and the unit change together on a graph. We derive Q = nu and n1u1 = n2u2 step by step, meet the seven SI base quantities, and see exactly why speed is derived: distance and time are base quantities, and speed is built by dividing one by the other. Side-by-side comparisons and two pause-and-think questions test base vs derived and scalar vs vector. Then a worked unit conversion, the exam trap about electric current, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.
